rationale: C13 is the very Panama Canal toll proclamation whose effective date the child postpones. The child repeats C13's statutory authority and expressly identifies the increased tolls, original October 1, 1948 effective date, and March 26, 1948 proclamation before replacing that effective date with April 1, 1949. This is direct reuse of both concrete language and the earlier directive's operative machinery. C19 and C08 are weaker analogues involving changes to the temporal or operative effect of earlier directives, but neither supplies the child's Panama Canal-specific material.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas section 411 of title 2 of the Canal Zone Code, approved June 19, 1934, authorizes the President to prescribe and from time to time change the tolls that shall be levied by the Government of the United States for the use of the Panama Canal
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas section 411 of title 2 of the Canal Zone Code, approved June 19, 1934, authorizes the President to prescribe and from time to time change the tolls that shall be levied by the Government of the United States for the use of the Panama Canal
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces the parent’s distinctive statutory-authority recital nearly verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas increased tolls were prescribed by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 26, 1948, the same proclamation to become effective on October 1, 1948
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This proclamation shall become effective on October 1, 1948
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly identifies C13 by its date and incorporates its operative effective date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the effective date of the said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 26, 1948, is postponed to, and shall be, April 1, 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This proclamation shall become effective on October 1, 1948
shared_material.explanation: The child directly modifies the central temporal provision of C13 while leaving its toll prescription intact.
